medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The Academic Assistance Program provides assistance to all students, as well as more personalized assistance to those needing more intensive help with their studies. This support is given in multiple formats: group sessions, one on one academic counseling, and online resources accessible to students at all times. Examples of foundational assistance include providing information on active study strategies, learning tools, and navigating medical school. Each student has a designated Learning Specialist who provides transitional support, such as developing a study schedule and adjusting to the volume and pace of learning in medical school. During more personalized meetings, Learning Specialists assist students with developing active study strategies and help them prepare for exams, including board exams. The program includes near-peer tutoring whereby 4th year students receive elective credit for providing 1:1 content support for both our curriculum and board exam preparation.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Commonly approved requests include requests to complete research or other fellowships, including the MU School of Medicine Post Sophomore Fellowship in Pathology and  health, personal, and childbirth or child care related leaves. Requests to delay graduation are rarely approved, and generally only for personal reasons, such as a student's wish to enter residency at the same time as a spouse or partner.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Many students join medical interest groups and local chapters of national medical organizations.  The groups typically meet at the beginning of each block and most meetings involve a lecture and meal. In Columbia most students volunteer at MedZou, our popular student run free health clinic, gives students the opportunity to serve those in our community without insurance.  Intramural sports and mentoring programs are very popular as well.
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
Beginning in 2027 the University of Missouri School of Medicine will have two campuses; one in Columbia, Missouri and one in Springfield, Missouri. Our Columbia campus is located in the heart of the University of Missouri flagship campus, and will admit 136 students. Columbia blends a thriving academic community with a growing regional health‑care network, making it a natural fit for a medical school that will shape the future of patient care. Our Springfield campus, located near the Ozark Greenways network, will welcome an inaugural class of 32 students. With strong hospital networks and a community that’s expanding every year, Springfield offers an ideal environment for training the next generation of medical professionals.

 The MU School of Medicine model explicitly focuses students’ attention on the people they are preparing to serve, and students’ clinically-based education will draw on the patient-centered care provided by CoxHealth, Mercy and University of Missouri Health Care.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Most medical students live in privately owned apartments, condominiums, and townhouses; some purchase their own homes. While on‑campus housing isn’t available at either location, both cities offer plenty of nearby apartments and neighborhoods close enough to campus and the hospitals for many students to bike or walk. The Office of Admissions creates a housing guide for all incoming students that offers comments from current medical students about various housing options in both Columbia and Springfield.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: We value the uniqueness of every individual and strive to ensure each person’s success. Contributions from individuals with a range of backgrounds, experiences and perspectives promote intellectual pluralism and enable us to achieve the excellence that we seek in learning, research, and engagement. This commitment makes our university a better place to work, learn and innovate.  The University of Missouri School of Medicine partners with the University of Missouri undergraduate campus to provide a safe and welcoming environment for all students.  The campus Office of Student Affairs serves as a valuable resource, providing student support to the many campus communities. To learn more about the services they provide please visit the website. https://studentaffairs.missouri.edu/resource-guide-for-students/
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The School of Medicine partners with the Disability Center on the main University of Missouri campus to support students needing classroom or exam accommodations to facilitate their academic success. Upon receiving a formal accommodations letter from the MU Disability Center, MUSOM works with the student to provide needed accommodations to reduce their risk of academic difficulties.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
All M1 and M2 students meet individually with the Faculty Director of Medical Student Well-being for mandatory 15-minute Health and Wellness check-ins. All medical students can email the Faculty Director of Medical Student Well-being to schedule additional meetings for support, mentoring, and to learn about available resources. Student requests for information are confidential and these meetings do not provide treatment.

The Mizzou Med Peer Support Program is committed to normalizing the discussion of academic stress, mental health, and other challenges that medical students face. Peer mentors are available to listen, provide support, and share information about resources. Students can connect with mentors who’ve had similar experiences.

The Missouri legislature passed Senate Bill 52 to bring awareness to medical student well-being, mental health, stress management, and student treatment. Show Me Compassionate Medical Education activities focus on helping students to connect and to raise awareness of mental health risks and resources. All MU medical students complete an M1 Wellness Orientation, and the online Ask Listen Refer suicide prevention training program. Students will be sent emails for upcoming Show-me Compassionate Medical Education events, Health and Wellness Block Talks, and other activities. Past activities have included wellness presentations, student and resident panels, yoga, mindfulness classes, and other fun activities.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
Our collaborative learning environment encourages students to work together across disciplines, fostering a spirit of teamwork and mutual support that mirrors the interdisciplinary nature of modern health care. Whether through hands-on clinical experiences, engaging in research with faculty mentors, or participating in community outreach initiatives, Mizzou Med students are prepared to become compassionate, culturally competent physicians who are equipped to address the evolving needs of the populations they serve.

The School of Medicine is also committed to supporting students' well-being. We recognize the challenges that come with pursuing a rigorous medical education, and we provide a variety of resources designed to promote mental and physical health, academic success, and personal growth. The sense of camaraderie and care within our medical community ensures that each student feels supported throughout their journey.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: For our Columbia campus, some clinical experiences will occur outside the medical school/main hospital. For our Springfield campus, all clinical experiences will occur outside the medical school. While public transit options are modest in both cities, rideshare services provide convenient transportation if needed.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Casual during small group, engaged learning sessions and lectures during the pre-clerkship phase. Professional dress during all clinical experiences, including those in the simulation center.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Students are welcome to schedule appointments with deans and staff to help answer their questions and to request support and resources. Tutoring may be available to students based on individual needs.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Early pre‑clerkship patient encounters help students connect basic science to clinical work and build skills that prepare them for the more demanding clinical phase of the curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Small group learning emphasizing clinical reasoning, basic sciences, self-directed learning, collaborative learning, and early clinical experiences.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: At this time, required clerkships are: Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Neurology, Obstetrics and Gynecology, Pediatrics, Psychiatry, and Surgery.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: Graduates are grouped according to their academic and clinical performance, level of participation in organizations, community service, research, leadership roles, and professionalism in med school.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Lectures provided to students are required for preparation to participate in required engaged learning activities (‘flipped classroom’ model). Didactics in the clinical phase are required.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: In 1993, The University of Missouri School of Medicine implemented a curriculum that substantially reduced lectures in favor of problem-based learning. Now called patient-based learning, our curriculum emphasizes problem solving, self-directed learning and early clinical experiences rather than memorization. The first and second years each consist of four 10-week blocks. The third year is made up of seven core clerkships completed at our Columbia or Springfield clinical campuses.  Some students may also complete clerkships as part of the Rural Scholars Program. The fourth year consists of advanced clinical selectives, advanced biomedical selectives and general electives. Students participate in robust simulation activities and assessments during all 4 years.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: The University of Missouri School of Medicine has ranked academic programs in family and community medicine and primary care.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: There is a required service-learning activity during the pre-clerkship phase of the curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: The University of Missouri Healthcare Hospitals and clinics, CoxHealth, Mercy Health Systems, Truman Veteran’s (Veterans') Affairs Hospital, and multiple community hospitals across the state.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem:
Pre-clerkship phase: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory

Clinical phase: Honors/Letters of Commendation/Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: As the first publicly supported medical school west of the Mississippi River, the University of Missouri School of Medicine has improved health, education and research since 1872. Mizzou Med is a pioneer in patient-centered learning style of medical education that emphasizes problem solving, self-directed learning and early clinical experience. More Missouri physicians received their medical degree from MU than from any other university. The School of Medicine’s more than 720 faculty physicians and scientists educate more than 1,000 medical students, residents, fellows and graduate-level learners.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: To save and improve lives – through exemplary education, research and patient care.
medSchoolInformation.videoDescription: Our medical school building at our Columbia campus.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
NON-TRADITIONAL APPLICANTS:
If the applicant has completed an undergraduate degree before September 2024, please have at least three letters of recommendation sent from individuals who are familiar with the applicant's recent scientific work, study experience or professional experience. A letter from a professor is NOT required, but will be accepted. 

TRADITIONAL APPLICANTS:
One letter from a professor who taught and issued the applicant a grade is required. It is strongly recommended that the letter from a professor who issued a grade be from science faculty. Letters from teaching assistants will not satisfy this requirement. Applicants may submit a pre-med committee or composite letter in lieu of the three individual letters. MU appreciates those who submit a pre-med committee letter as well as individual letters.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: Letter writers please provide an accurate assessment of the applicant’s suitability for medical school rather than advocate for the applicant. Focus on behaviors you have observed directly when describing an applicant’s suitability for medical school, as well as including unique contributions that an applicant would bring to an incoming class. Please note that we do not share anything mentioned in letters with the applicants.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: Invites to interview will start going out late September and will continue to be sent out through February. We do rolling admissions interview offers.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Two open file, one-on-one interviews by Admissions Committee members are required, as well attendance at various presentations (typical interview day is 3 hours).
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Qualified and competitive applicants will receive a secondary application. Non-MO residents may be invited to submit a prelim Out-Of-State form to determine if a secondary application will be offered.
medSchoolApplication.secApplEarliestDtText: Secondaries will be sent out after July 6, 2026. They can be submitted as soon as they are completed.
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: To apply for the early-decision program, candidates must have a cumulative undergraduate GPA of at least 3.75 and a MCAT of 508. Only in-state residents may apply through this program.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: Must be U.S. citizen or permanent resident. OOS applicants must meet certain MCAT and undergraduate cumulative GPA combinations to be considered, as well as have significant ties to the state.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: OOS applicants must meet certain MCAT and undergraduate cumulative GPA combinations to be considered. More information: https://medicine.missouri.edu/education/admissions/md-application-requirements
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
ACADEMIC REQUIREMENTS:
MCAT- MCAT must be taken between January 2023 and September 2026. To be considered for entry in 2027, applicants must provide scores from exams administered through September 2026. Candidates must earn an MCAT score of at least 500  to be considered.

GPA - All applicants must have an overall cumulative and science GPA of a 3.0 or higher. The Admissions Committee will not consider applicants with either a science cumulative or an overall cumulative GPA of less than 3.0, unless the applicant also has significant post-baccalaureate or graduate coursework. A competitive applicant would need to have well above the minimum in either their MCAT score or GPA. Meeting only the minimum requirements in both areas is unlikely to result in a successful application.

OOS APPLICANTS - Applicants who do not have a legal residence of Missouri on their AMCAS application are welcome to apply. Since the MU School of Medicine is a state funded university, the majority of accepted students (around 80-85%) will have a legal residence of Missouri. Due to a high number of out-of-state applications, OOS applicants must meet certain MCAT and undergraduate cumulative GPA combinations to be considered. If an applicant has taken significant post-baccalaureate or graduate coursework, the graduate cumulative GPA will be considered individually if academic combinations are not met. If applicants meet the academic requirements, they will be emailed an Out-Of-State form (no cost), this form determines the applicants' ties to the state of Missouri. If the Out-Of-State form is approved, a secondary application will be provided.

COURSEWORK REQUIREMENTS - Applicants must have completed at least 90 semester hours from a U.S. college or university. All required coursework must also be taken at a U.S. college or university.
Required coursework with a grade of C- or better:
College English composition or writing intensive, six credit hours or one year
Mathematics (college algebra or above), three credit hours or one semester
Biologic sciences (e.g., biology, genetics, cell biology, animal physiology, molecular biology, histology), six credit hours or one year
Chemistry (through organic chemistry), twelve credit hours or two years
General physics, six credit hours or one year

medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: The MCAT results and academic record assist the committee in evaluating an individual’s aptitude for medical education. Equally important, however, are the applicant’s personal characteristics and experiences related to health care. We take a holistic approach to admissions and evaluate the entire application; academics, Missouri affiliation, personal statement, altruism and leadership experiences, health care experiences, research, as well the applicant’s experiences that demonstrate an appreciation of social factors that influence health. All of those areas will be reviewed to determine who receives an interview invite.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: Applicants must score at least a 500 to be considered. Out-of-State applicants applicants must meet certain MCAT and undergraduate cumulative GPA combinations to be considered.

The Admissions Committee will not consider applicants with either a science cumulative or an overall cumulative GPA of less than 3.0, unless the applicant also has significant post-baccalaureate or graduate coursework. Out-of-State applicants applicants must meet certain MCAT and undergraduate cumulative GPA combinations to be considered.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: A competitive applicant would need to have well above the minimum in either their MCAT score or GPA. Meeting only the minimum requirements in both areas is unlikely to result in a successful application.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We accept community college courses as long as they meet our general requirements. For specific questions regarding credit, reach out to the admissions office directly.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo:
We only accept application updates prior to an interview offer. Once an applicant interviews we do not accept update letters. 

We do not accept letters of intent OR letters of interest at any stage in the application cycle.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Due of our obligation to ensure that patients receive highly effective medical care, certain abilities are required of our students. All students of medicine must possess those intellectual, emotional, social and physical capabilities necessary to participate fully in the curriculum and which are essential to achieve the levels of competence required by the faculty. Students must be able to meet the technical standards with or without accommodation, for successful completion. Students will be asked to attest to the technical standards every year.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Students are admitted to the School of Medicine without regard to financial circumstances. MU participates in federal loan programs as well as providing assistance from institutional loan and scholarship programs. Students receive aid based on merit, financial need, or both with funding coming from a variety of sources such as school, federal, and private sources.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: All students enrolled at the University of Missouri are required to pay tuition based on the number of credits of instruction they are receiving.  Other required fees include the prepaid health fee, recreation facility fee, student activity fee, information technology fee, and the medical resource fee for medical students. All fees are due and payable to the University and are the student's responsibility to pay as the result of registration or other activity that incurred as charges to the student. A minimum payment option is available for students unable to complete their financial arrangements at the time of registration.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
The Tom and Anne Smith MD-PhD Program allows students to receive training in a comprehensive program to prepare dual-degree physician-scientists for a career in academic medicine. MD-PhD students pursue a seven- to eight-year course of study that combines the traditional four years of medical school with the three to four years typically required to earn a doctorate in a scientific discipline. 

Physician-scientists who complete the MD-PhD program are uniquely prepared to lead independent research programs and train others in translational bench-to-bedside research. They are also able to provide exceptional patient care to assimilate the latest scientific knowledge to the practice of medicine.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Applicants are notified about their placement on the waitlist at the end of interview season. Applicants are notified of acceptance on the day that someone withdraws up until the first day of class.

medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: There is no date restriction - coursework can be completed at any time.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
Once an applicant is offered an interview, they will then be interviewed by members of the Admissions Committee which is comprised of students, faculty, and alumni. The Admissions Committee uses letters of evaluation, pre-medical community and educational activities, and the interview to assess the extent to which the applicant has the personal characteristics and knowledge of health care to adequately commit to a lifelong career as a patient-centered physician. The Admissions Committee will determine if an applicant will be admitted, on the alternate list, or denied once all the interviews are completed.

MD-PhD applicants will be offered admission based on a decision from both the MD and PhD Admissions Committees, and will only be considered for the MD-PhD dual program.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Competitive applicants will have various shadowing experiences throughout different specialties.
